## Round 1 (gen1) findings: q09 specialisation
- Baseline q09 was about 918-980 ms. The old plan built hash tables on 15M orders and 8M partsupp. The LIKE contains filter got 0.2 selectivity.
- E0001 ACCEPTED: STRING_PATTERN_SELECTIVITY 0.05 in relation_statistics_helper.cpp ExtractGetStats. q09 went 980 to 723 ms (1.254x).
- BuildProbeSideOptimizer (build_probe_side_optimizer.cpp TryFlipJoinChildren) compares row_width*cardinality, with penalties for VARCHAR/column count and PREFER_RIGHT_DEEP_PENALTY.
- InspectTableFilter only handles CONSTANT_COMPARISON equality and AND.
- SQL experiment trick: SET disabled_optimizers='join_order,build_side_probe_side' plus explicit JOINs (left=probe, right=build).

## Round 2 findings (plan after E0001, q09.m0 EXPLAIN ANALYZE about 1.05s)
- Plan: part(filter, 109K) ⋈ partsupp (436K) is the build side of the 2-key join with lineitem (l_partkey, l_suppkey). That join takes 2.27s; the lineitem scan emits 60M rows (2.74s) with only min/max dynamic filters. Then the orders join (1.74s, builds on 3.27M, probes 15M orders) and supplier⋈nation (tiny). HASH_GROUP_BY 0.16s, compress projection 0.14s.
- Why no BF: CanUseBloomFilter (physical_hash_join.cpp ~761) requires ht->conditions.size()==1. The JoinHashTable BF is filled in Finalize (join_hashtable.cpp ~775) from the stored combined row hash (pointer_offset), so it only matches a single-key probe hash. The probe side is BFTableFilter::HashInternal = VectorOperations::Hash(column).
- BF pushes are deferred until HashJoinFinalizeEvent (deferred_bloom_filters). They are wrapped in SelectivityOptionalFilter (BF_THRESHOLD), so a useless BF switches itself off.
- build_side_has_filter = IsFiltering(child), which recurses, so a join build side that contains a filtered GET counts as filtered.
- TupleDataCollection::Gather(row_locations, sel, count, column_id, result, target_sel, cached_cast) exists (tuple_data_collection.hpp:213).
- DISPATCHED r2: a multi-key BF built on the hash of key column 0 only.

## Tool notes
- dbe-tool sql output of wide EXPLAIN trees is hard to grep; grep "Total Time" for timing.
- `dbe-tool profile q09.m0 | grep -E "rows|[0-9]s|Table:|Conditions|="` gives a usable plan summary.
- profile.md truncates the right side of the plan; run profile yourself.
- Bash won't run commands containing $VAR expansions; inline the full paths.

## Directions
- Next if the BF lands: the orders join (1.74s) probes 15M orders against a 3.27M build. A BF on o_orderkey might help a little (3.27M lineitems map to many orders, maybe 20%+ of orders, so weak). Check if the min/max filter prunes.
- Backlog: multi-key join estimate (cardinality_estimator.cpp). Less relevant now that the build side flipped correctly.
- Later: compress/decompress projections around the aggregate (0.14s), HASH_GROUP_BY 0.16s.

issues.title: Bloom filter pushdown for multi-key hash joins on the first key
issues.hypothesis: After E0001 the q09 plan joins lineitem to (partsupp⋈part, 436K rows) on two keys: l_partkey=p_partkey AND l_suppkey=ps_suppkey. The profile shows the lineitem TABLE_SCAN emitting 59,986,046 rows (2.74s cumulative) with only min/max dynamic filters, and the 2-key HASH_JOIN at 2.27s probing 60M rows to produce 3.27M. No bloom filter is pushed because JoinFilterPushdownInfo::CanUseBloomFilter (physical_hash_join.cpp:775) requires ht->conditions.size()==1. That check exists because the hash table's row hash combines all keys, so a probe side that hashes one column can't test it. If we build a separate bloom filter from the hash of the first key column alone (VectorOperations::Hash of that column, which is exactly what BFTableFilter::HashInternal computes on the probe side), the scan can drop about 95% of lineitem rows early. Before E0001 the BF on l_partkey cut lineitem to 3.45M rows. So the new plan plus that BF should take most of the 2.7s scan and 2.3s join time out of the query.
issues.plan: 1) In physical_hash_join.cpp CanUseBloomFilter: allow conditions.size()>1 when the filter being pushed is for condition index 0 (pass filter_idx in, or check it in FinalizeFilters at line 899), as long as that condition is COMPARE_EQUAL. Keep the other checks (build_side_has_filter, probe>build, no perfect HT, no cast). 2) In join_hashtable.cpp: when should_build_bloom_filter is set and conditions.size()>1, JoinHashTable::Finalize (line 775) should not insert the stored combined row hashes into bloom_filter in InsertHashes. Instead, for each chunk, gather key column 0 from row_locations using data_collection->Gather(row_locations_vector, sel, count, column_id=0, key_vector, sel, nullptr) (tuple_data_collection.hpp:213; the key columns come first in the layout), run VectorOperations::Hash(key_vector, hashes, count), then bloom_filter.InsertHashes(hashes, count). The single-key path stays unchanged. 3) PushBloomFilter already uses conditions[0] for key name, type and NullValuesAreEqual(0), so it stays correct. Before the change, check that the multi-key HT row hash is not what the BF probe expects anywhere else (e.g. a probe-side BF check in JoinHashTable::Probe using bloom_filter on the combined hash). Grep join_hashtable.cpp for bloom_filter uses. If the HT itself probes the BF with combined hashes, keep that path disabled for multi-key or use a separate BloomFilter member for pushdown.
issues.expected_gain: q09: lineitem rows into the 2-key join should drop from 60M to about 3.5M. Expect 30-50% on q09 (725ms to about 400-500ms).
issues.generality: Any star or snowflake query that joins a large fact table to a filtered dimension or bridge on a composite key (e.g. fact ⋈ partsupp-like tables on 2 FKs, or multi-column date/key joins). SelectivityOptionalFilter switches the BF off at runtime when it doesn't filter, so non-selective first keys cost only the sampled checks plus the build-side gather and hash (small, build is the smaller side). Joins that could get slower: multi-key joins with a large build side, which pay an extra gather and hash pass at finalize.
issues.risk: Medium. Correctness depends on the BF hash matching the probe-side hash exactly (same column type, same VectorOperations::Hash). A mismatch would wrongly drop rows, so test multi-key joins, including NULL keys, a VARCHAR first key and an external/partitioned hash join. The has_cast check must stay.
